title: Benchmarking hygiene and stable-pinning operations for model onboarding
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Objective: Define and operationalize a repeatable 'benchmarking hygiene' checklist and a stable-pinning operations workflow that produces Redwood-verified performance profiles (latency/throughput/cost) suitable for publishing to the performance catalog.

Background: Model onboarding currently produces perf profiles with varying degrees of artifact quality. We see drift from stale test harnesses, inconsistent sampling, and missing cost baselines. This ticket captures the product-level requirements and acceptance criteria for a hygiene checklist plus the operational flow to pin a model version as 'stable' in the catalog.

Scope (in-scope):
- Minimum benchmarking hygiene checks to pass before a profile can be published (see acceptance criteria).
- A deterministic pinning operation that creates a signed, git-backed profile artifact referencing exact model build, quantization, kernel selection, and infra flavor.
- A staging-to-prod publish flow that supports canary sampling and automatic backout if regressions are detected.
- Operational metadata to surface in Console (expected latency p50/p95, throughput for target batch sizes, cost-per-1k-tokens baseline, test harness commit SHA).

Out of scope: reworking model training pipelines, deep changes to runtime kernels (handled by ENG follow-ups).

Acceptance criteria: 
1) A profiling run template (harness) exists in the onboarding repo and can be executed via CI to generate a reproducible profile. Template includes seed control, warmup token handling, and a calibrated user workload distribution file.
2) Profiles include: model sha, quantization flavor, sequence length buckets, batch-size throughput curves, p50/p95 latency, 99th percentile memory, and cost-per-1k tokens.
3) Publishing flow creates a git-tagged, signed artifact stored in the profile registry and populates the performance catalog with metadata and sample telemetry links.
4) Canary publish runs a 1% production-sampled traffic route for 24 hours with automated comparison to pinned baseline; regressions trigger rollback and уведомление to on-call and PM assignee.
5) Console surfaces 'verified at' timestamp, profiling commit, and TTL (time-to-live) for auto-refresh.

Proposed flow: 
1) Author runs the CI profiling job against a staging deployment (harness: onboarding/profiles/harness.yaml).
2) CI outputs profile JSON and a human-readable report; both are uploaded to the profile-registry repo and a git tag is created: profiles/{model}:{version}:{profile-sha}.
3) PM/Tech-reviewer approves via GitHub review; approval triggers Publisher job to sign artifact (GPG/KMS) and add to Catalog with 'candidate' status.
4) Automated canary policy runs for 24 hours and emits a pass/fail signal. If pass, status flips to 'stable' and profile is pinned. If fail, publisher auto-rolls back and opens ENG incident if regression severity >= medium.

Trade-offs considered: 
- Full automation vs manual gating: Full automation speeds onboarding but increases risk of noisy publishes. We adopt a hybrid: automated generation + manual approval for first-time model families, then progressively more automation for repeatable families.
- Tight acceptance bar vs time-to-publish: stricter checks improve user trust but slow releases. We recommend a critical-path checklist with optional enhanced checks for premium models.

Telemetry & monitoring:
- Grafana dashboard: perf/profile-registry overview (link in comments).
- Alerting: regression-alert if p95 latency increases by >15% or cost-per-1k increases by >10% compared to pinned baseline.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: Merge harness template and publisher job in onboarding repo; docs for profiling run.
- Week 2: Implement git-backed signing and candidate publish flow; manual approval experiment for 2 model families.
- Week 3: Enable 24h canary for candidate publishes and automated pass/fail evaluation; add Console metadata surfaces.
- Week 4: Move to 'stable' pinning for families that pass repeated vetting; document TTL and refresh cadence.

Acceptance test examples: 
- Run profiling CI on small LLM (open-7B) with sequence lengths [64,256,1024], batch sizes [1,8,32] and confirm throughput curves generated and cost baseline recorded.
- Trigger a canary with a known regression (inject 20% added latency) and confirm rollback and alerting.

Documentation & artifacts:
- Profiling harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboarding/pull/312
- Draft publishing playbook (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Publishing+Performance+Profiles+Playbook
- Registry repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/profile-registry

Open questions: 
- Should TTL for auto-refresh be model-family specific? Recommendation: default 90 days, allow overrides for enterprise customers.
- What is the minimum sample size and duration for canaries for large models under low traffic? (ENG to propose sampling heuristics).

Next steps:
- ENG: implement canary comparison job and regression detector (ENG-9421).
- DX: add Console metadata tiles and links to profile artifacts (DES-2043).
- Security: validate signing approach with KMS/HSM and produce threat model (security review not required for initial MVP).
